questions.stem: What is the difference between a strong acid and a weak acid?

options.text: A strong acid is more concentrated than a weak acid
A strong acid fully ionises in water; a weak acid only partially ionises
A strong acid reacts with metals; a weak acid does not
A strong acid has a higher boiling point than a weak acid

questions.explanation: A strong acid fully dissociates (ionises) in water, releasing all its H⁺ ions. A weak acid only partially ionises, so fewer H⁺ ions are released into solution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid that fully ionises in water: HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻. Ethanoic acid, citric acid, and carbonic acid are all weak acids.

questions.stem: A strong acid at the same concentration as a weak acid will have:
questions.explanation: At the same concentration, a strong acid has a lower pH because it fully ionises, producing more H⁺ ions than a weak acid of the same concentration, which only partially ionises.

questions.stem: Why is 'strong' not the same as 'concentrated' when describing acids?

options.text: They actually mean the same thing
'Strong' refers to how completely the acid ionises; 'concentrated' refers to how much acid is dissolved per unit volume
'Concentrated' means the acid is more dangerous
'Strong' means the acid has a higher boiling point

questions.explanation: 'Strong' describes the degree of ionisation (fully or partially). 'Concentrated' describes the amount of acid dissolved in a given volume. A dilute strong acid and a concentrated weak acid are different things.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a weak acid commonly found in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) is a weak acid found in vinegar. It only partially ionises in water, making it much less corrosive than strong acids.

questions.stem: How would the rate of reaction with magnesium compare for equal concentrations of hydrochloric acid (strong) and ethanoic acid (weak)?

options.text: Both would react at the same rate

questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid would react faster because, as a strong acid, it produces more H⁺ ions at the same concentration. More H⁺ ions means more collisions with the magnesium, giving a faster rate.

questions.stem: The ionisation of a weak acid in water is best described as:

options.text: A reversible process that reaches equilibrium
A process that does not produce any H⁺ ions
A process that requires a catalyst

questions.explanation: Weak acids partially ionise in a reversible process. An equilibrium is established between the undissociated acid molecules and the ions, with the position lying to the left (mostly undissociated).
